categories.main_business_segments: Cirrus Logic operates in one reportable segment but reports revenue in two primary product lines: Audio Products and High-Performance Mixed-Signal Products. Audio Products include boosted amplifiers, codecs, smart codecs, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters, and standalone digital signal processors. High-Performance Mixed-Signal Products encompass camera controllers, haptic driver and sensing solutions, power conversion and control ICs, and fast-charging ICs.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing, leveraging advanced analog and digital signal processing technologies. As a fabless semiconductor company, Cirrus Logic outsources wafer fabrication to foundries such as TSMC and GlobalFoundries, and contracts third parties for assembly and testing. Their products often integrate proprietary hardware with embedded software and algorithms, including programmable features and IP from both internal and third-party sources.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cirrus Logic's key customers are leading global electronics manufacturers, with Apple Inc. accounting for approximately 79% of total sales in fiscal 2022. The company serves markets including smartphones, tablets, laptops, AR/VR headsets, home theater systems, automotive entertainment, and professional audio systems, with a strong focus on mobile and consumer electronics.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with major offices and technical support centers in the United States, United Kingdom, China, South Korea, Japan, Singapore, and Taiwan. In fiscal 2022, 98% of net sales were international, with significant revenue from China, Hong Kong, Vietnam, South Korea, and the rest of the world.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cirrus Logic is a fabless semiconductor company, operating downstream in the supply chain. It focuses on IC design and development, relying on third-party foundries for wafer fabrication and external vendors for assembly and testing, before delivering finished components to OEMs and contract manufacturers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Cirrus Logic aims to maintain leadership in smartphone audio, expand audio component sales beyond smartphones, and grow its high-performance mixed-signal product line into adjacent markets. The company invests heavily in R&D (23% of sales in FY22), focusing on advanced mixed-signal design, low-power processing, and new product development, including power management and fast-charging solutions following the Lion Semiconductor acquisition.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of proprietary semiconductor components to OEMs, contract manufacturers, and distributors. Sales are made via both direct and indirect channels, with most transactions based on short-term purchase orders rather than long-term contracts.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Cirrus Logic faces competition from both large and emerging semiconductor companies, including AKM Semiconductor, Analog Devices, Goodix Technology, Qualcomm, Realtek, Renesas, Richtek, Skyworks, ST Microelectronics, Synaptics, and Texas Instruments. The company is a leading supplier in audio and high-performance mixed-signal ICs, particularly in mobile devices, but operates in highly competitive and rapidly evolving markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2022, Cirrus Logic reported record net sales of $1.78 billion, up 30% from $1.37 billion in 2021, with net income of $326 million and a gross margin of 51.8%. The company has demonstrated strong growth, especially in high-performance mixed-signal products (124% YoY growth in FY22), and maintains a robust balance sheet with significant cash reserves and no outstanding debt under its $300 million revolving credit facility.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cirrus Logic differentiates itself through expertise in low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing, delivering highly integrated, programmable, and software-enhanced ICs that enable innovative user experiences. The company emphasizes close engineering collaboration with customers, proprietary IP, and the ability to deliver custom and general market solutions that meet demanding technical and price requirements, particularly for leading-edge mobile and consumer applications.
